critical_code_review_comments: projects.py (~700 lines) mixes projects, tasks, help_requests, task_history — split into modules (projects.py, tasks.py, help.py) once it grows further

list_projects builds an $and around visible_project_filter's own $or; works but nested filters could be simplified. Also 'overdue' adds a duplicate 'status' key that gets overwritten by the earlier status filter — low impact but worth simplifying

professionals.get_professional pops 3 admin-only keys but forgets 'documents' and 'promo_codes' which may contain contract-related info; consider a whitelist rather than blacklist for non-admin fields

imports_csv.execute reads file.read() twice implicitly (analyze then execute) — client uploads twice, which is fine, but ensure large-file handling is documented. Also file.read() has no size limit → risk of DoS on very large CSVs
help-requests PUT accepts a raw dict payload instead of a Pydantic model — inconsistent with the rest of the API and skips validation
notify_bureau() iterates all admins per action; fine at low volume but O(admins) per event; consider a broadcast collection or a single 'BUREAU' recipient
Same Phase-1 comment still applies: CORS allow_origins='*' with credentials, server.py still >700 lines
test_credentials: See /app/memory/test_credentials.md — all credentials validated during tests.
seed_data_creation: Tests use only 'TEST_' prefixed projects/tasks/help_requests and always cascade-delete their parent project at end. CSV import creates one new user test_new_import@example.com (ACTIVE, imported=true) — safe to keep or archive.
